# Flat Wire Planning — Change Log

**Project:** Flat Wire Mill Implementation
**Document Type:** Consolidated change log — the single home for document change history
**Last Updated:** August 25, 2026 — **`FW-138` built and verified** (22 endpoints, 56/56 cases, 22/22 `401`, new decision `P-55`); `FW-138`'s `P-53` (no `/rod/**` surface) carried through the documents of record and into `ual-api`, where `RodReceivingController.cs` is deleted and the solution rebuilds clean; its propagation across six sibling plans; nine Repository-wide rows for the `LatestDocument/` → `MVP-1/ProjectPlan/` sync; the five double-sectioned documents flagged and the 27 with no section recorded *(previously August 23, 2026)*
**Status:** Active — append here, never to an individual document

---

## How this file works

**This is the only change log in the repository.** On 12 Aug 2026 the per-document
`## Change Log` sections were removed from all 63 documents that carried one and their
entries moved here **verbatim**. Do not add a `## Change Log` section to any document —
append a row to the relevant section below instead.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Where entries go** | Under the `##` heading naming the document they describe. Add the document's section if it has none yet, in repository path order. |
| **Cross-document changes** | Under [Repository-wide](#repository-wide), not repeated under each file touched. |
| **Documents with two sections** | Five have one under their **former** name and one under their current path — `Architecture.md`, `APIs.md`, `REVIEW.md`, `Roadmap.md`, `SprintPlan.md`. Both are kept, because a heading names the document as it stood. **Append to the later of the two**; each pair carries a note saying which. |
| **Documents with no section** | **27 files under `MVP-1/ProjectPlan/` have none**, including **phase files `03`–`11`, `13` and `14`** (only `01a`/`01b`/`01c` and `12` have one), all three `Frontend/` documents, three `Operations/`, three `Testing/`, `PLCTagSpecification.md`, `ExceptionHandling.md` and the `FW-219`/`220`/`223` plans. Their history lives in their own `**Last Updated:**` header trails and under Repository-wide. **Create the section on the next material change** — do not back-fill empty ones. *(Counted 25 Aug 2026.)* |
| **Entries are verbatim** | Dates, wording and column shapes are exactly as migrated. Several entries deliberately cite **superseded** numbering, values and filenames — that is the audit trail, not an error. Read each against the reading note in its section. |
| **Document headers still apply** | Each document keeps its **Project / Last Updated / Status** header block. Update `Last Updated` on the document *and* append the entry here. |
| **Versions live in the Version column** | The thirteen client-review specifications in `MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/Screens/` are versioned. Their sections carry a **`Version`** column; stamp the new version on the row you append, and set the same value in the document's `**Version:**` header. A row that records no version bump carries `—`. |

**The `MVP-1/` client-review specifications no longer carry a `## Document Change History`
block — removed 15 Aug 2026.** All thirteen blocks were deleted and their 39 version rows
folded into the sections below, which is why those sections have a `Version` column. The
`.docx` deliverables no longer print a history section; a specification states its version
in its header block and nowhere else, and this file is the only record of how it got there.
**`MVP-2/RequirementDocuments/` was out of scope for that pass** — its four specifications
(`DieManagement`, `PassScheduleGenerationSpec`, `PassScheduleManagement`, `ShiftSummary`)
still carry their own blocks. `RollAdjust.md` §6 *Change History* and the *Change History
Panel* section of the dashboard design reference are **not change logs and were not
touched** — the first describes a panel in the Roll Adjust dialog listing prior gap
adjustments, the second describes a screen.

> **Load-bearing content lives in this file.** Three things that other documents cite by
> name are change-log entries, and their citations now resolve here:
> the **`Q##` old→new renumbering map** (12 Aug 2026) and the **`[PLC]` v1.0 section and
> `PLC-Q##` mapping tables** (4 Aug 2026), both under
> [`Analysis/FlatWireOpenQuestions.md`](#analysisflatwireopenquestionsmd); and the
> **superseded table-count history** under
> [`LatestDocument/FlatWire_MasterSpecification.md`](#latestdocumentflatwire_masterspecificationmd).

> **Seven Database sections carry `MVP-1/DBChanges/…` display text from before the 13 August 2026
> restructure, and that is deliberate.** The hrefs are correct and current; only the visible label is
> stale. They are frozen because the GitHub-generated **anchor slug** is derived from the display
> text, and those slugs are linked from the `## Index` above and from outside this file — retitling
> them would silently break both. The same reasoning keeps `REVIEW.md`'s old file names.

Putting it in `MVP-1/SRS/` would place an unguarded file among guarded ones. Two properties keep the expansion safe: **single pass** over one longest-first alternation, so a replacement's output cannot be re-matched; and **no replacement contains its own key**, which is what makes it idempotent and why phrase entries exist. The guard's token set is **deliberately wider** than the expander's — `EF`, `DI`, `PWA` and `JWT` appear only inside phrases, so a bare one in new prose is flagged rather than expanded into something clumsy. `Phase 1A` and `Sprint 1` are exempt as identifiers, and code identifiers are untouched because `\bPLC\b` does not match `PLCTagService`.<br><br>**Five fatal guards, and every one was proved live by breaking it**: reconciliation (*"block table: computed 779, the plan prints 778"*), coverage, title resolution, drift, and abbreviation. Each run named the offending location and left no workbook on disk. Two findings worth keeping: the tables' **footer rows are excluded from their own sums on purpose** — counting them double-counts the total, which is why testing reconciliation means changing a *data* row; and injecting a bare `RT` did **not** trip the guard because the expander correctly handled it, so the real test uses a token the guard covers and the expander deliberately does not. |

| Jul 30, 2026 | Analysis team | Added **Q75** — whether multiple rod bundles can be **stacked on a single VPS payoff position**. Every artifact assumes one bundle per bay (`UX_RodStaging_Bay` enforces it as a filtered unique index), but nothing states whether that is the equipment's limit or a modelling assumption, and eye-to-sky is the geometry in which stacking is standard practice. The resolving fact — received bundle gross weight — is stated **two incompatible ways** in the delivered contracts: **8,690–8,840 lb** in `/payoff/status`, `/staging/queue` and `/staging/rod` versus **2,000 lb** in `/rod/{alpha}` and `/checkin/rod`, against a 9,000 lb position rating. That contradiction matters independently of stacking, because the payoff weight bar and the weld alerts (warn 3,000 lb / critical 2,000 lb) are calibrated to it. Recorded the four schema consequences if stacking is real, and flagged **`CK_WeldEvent_PayoffDiff`** as worth relaxing pre-emptively — it rejects an in-stack weld outright, and the real invariant is that the rod *alphas* differ, not the bays. Total questions: 75. |

| Aug 1, 2026 | Project decision | **Weld quality is captured at the weld; `Q24` widened.** Dashboard 2A's Mark as welded dialog now requires a **Pass/Fail** result with a reason mandatory on Fail (`WLD013`), using the same six reasons as Dashboard 4 — so one physical join is documented identically wherever it is captured. Quality was the only NOT NULL `WeldEvent` column that dialog lacked, so **`POST /weldevent` becomes the single weld write** and `POST /staging/rod/mark-welded` is **retired**; the `RodStaging` weld columns are set in the same transaction, **on a Pass only**. This closes `WeldEventPopupPlan` **Q-W1** ("is a quality result at weld time acceptable on the floor?" — yes) and confirms its decision **D-A**; it needs **no schema change**. **A failing weld does not mark the rod welded** — the join did not hold, so the position keeps reading *not yet welded*, the station states the failure and its reason, and the operator remakes the weld. That last rule **widens Q24** rather than adding a question: a remade weld leaves **several `WeldEvent` rows for one physical join**, which is the re-weld-on-certificate question Q24 already asks — now reachable two ways (a weld that breaks mid-run, and a weld that fails its quality check before anything runs through it). | Aug 6, 2026 | Analysis team | **Second gap audit of `PassScheduleGenerationSpec.md` — eighteen defects, seven algorithmic; specification at v1.5.** Again no `Q##` opens or closes, but **`Q97` and `Q98` are both widened** and **eight more `PSG-` items** are owed. The recurring cause was a change made in one section between 1 and 6 Aug and never carried into the sections that consume it. **The seven that mattered: (1) width was designed at one point on the line and nowhere else** — the entry diameter was solved from target width, then nothing computed width through FM2, although two later steps required it. New §3.3.12 and Step 9B do, and they surface a consequence no artifact had stated: **there is no edger at the mill exit, so final width leaves S3, which spreads** — the last edger must be set *narrow* of target or every FL2/FL3 coil runs over-width. **`PSG-D08` is therefore not an FL1-only item**, and S3's exit must be instrumented in the same trial campaign as FM1's. **(2)** Steps 9/9A/9B are **mutually dependent** and were written sequentially — now one iterative solve. **(3)** Step 9 had **no form for the FL2 path v1.4 had just added**, solving for an FM1 exit gauge that does not exist on FL2; split into rod and spool directions, with `k_bulk = 0` handled and a **pre-anneal** branch added, since *"intermediate anneal"* is meaningless with no upstream stage. **(4) An undersize rod passed silently** — a rod smaller than the required entry gives a *negative* area reduction, which satisfied the no-draw branch, so both draw boxes bypassed and a warning-free schedule issued for a product that cannot be made. **(5) The bite condition was the wrong relation on the wrong coefficient** — `PSG-D04` asked one number for die/wire *and* roll/material contact, and the limit is **quadratic in μ**; split, with rolling friction as **`PSG-D31`** (High). The flat-entry relation also **rejects the spec's own nominal example** when applied to FM1's round entry (it would need μ ≥ 0.176), so it is excluded and the real criterion asked as **`PSG-Q32`** (High). **(6)** Drive power, tension and `Q_p` were **required but not calculable** — no torque relation existed behind an Error-severity check, `R34` was tagged `[INDUSTRY STANDARD]` with no relation named, and `Q_p` had no source and no id. **(7) Cold work under-reported** — the area ratio equals the *length* strain alone, so v1.3's edger term was understated ~2×; equivalent strain now used for rolling and edging, and `ε_prior` added, which the formula had omitted although §4.2 makes it mandatory. **Also:** Step 12A split orders against take-up **ratings** rather than the **planned output multiple** this same call corroborated (`D8` — ~1,800 lb FL1, 800/900 FL2), roughly halving the reported unit count — now **`PSG-D32`**; §8 gained a third outcome (*not evaluated*), since a strict Error/Warning rule means no schedule could be approved at go-live; §8.7 held **fifteen rows against forty validations** and is completed, including `V27`, an **Error** blocked on `PSG-D26` and previously unlisted. New client items: **`PSG-D31`**–**`PSG-D35`**, **`PSG-Q32`**–**`PSG-Q34`**. **Separately, the audit found `FR-381`/`384`/`385`/`386`/`387` contradict this specification on five counts of physics** — recorded as `FlatWire_MasterSpecification.md` **§10.5** and a `REVIEW.md` Tier 1 callout, **not** in the client deliverable, which carries no requirement IDs. Re-rendered to `PassScheduleGenerationSpec.docx`. Totals unchanged: 99 · 50 Open/In Progress · 21 Decided · 1 Superseded. |

## [BaseDocuments/FL Alphas Plus - Analysis.md](BaseDocuments/FL%20Alphas%20Plus%20-%20Analysis.md)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 21, 2026 | Initial document, with the **recovered VBA source** filed beside it as `FL Alphas Plus - Module1.bas` (561 lines, verbatim) and the extractor committed as [`Tools/extract_vba.py`](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/extract_vba.py) — verified to reproduce the `.bas` byte-for-byte. `FL Alphas Plus.xlsm` (Tim O'Brien, 25 May 2026) is the tool referenced on the 20 Aug call, and it turns out to be **the only end-to-end implementation of the rod → spool → coil chain that exists anywhere**, in this repository or the delivered contracts.<br><br>⚠ **Recovering it is not a one-liner and the failure mode is silent.** The module text sits at **offset 22177** behind a ~22 KB performance cache, and a scan for the `0x01` container signature finds a **false start at offset 61** that decompresses without error and looks like valid source for several hundred bytes before degrading. The offset must come from the `dir` stream's `MODULEOFFSET` record, which is itself compressed. That is written into both the analysis doc and the tool's docstring, because anyone re-deriving this will hit the same trap.<br><br>**The alpha scheme is derivational and recursive, and it is a third candidate the alpha-format table does not record.** `R00001` → spool `R00001A` → stop `R00001AA`, each generation appending `AlphaLetter(n)` (Excel-column base-26, so 27 → `AA`). **A welded spool carries one alpha per segment in a single cell**, joined by `" - "` — `R00001C - R00002A` — while `" / "` joins consumption facts. ⚠ **The concatenated form is ambiguous by construction**: `R00001AA` is *either* "rod 1 → spool A → stop A" *or* "rod 1 → 27th segment", and it collides outright past 26 segments. `BusinessRules.md` §3.3 records a two-way `SP-#####` / `TS######` conflict; it is three-way, and the third option differs in **cardinality**, not just format.<br><br>**`SegmentType`'s four fields — `Rod`, `Alpha`, `Weight`, `SpoolID` — are confirmed by the client (21 Aug 2026) as their working data structure.** ⚠ **There is not one footage variable in 561 lines**: the client's model is **weight-primary**, which inverts any design that treats footage as the backbone and weight as deferred.<br><br>**Two rules the code states that no repository artifact does.** `' A STOP MAY USE MULTIPLE ALPHAS BUT ONLY FROM THE SAME SPOOL` — enforced by the loop, so **a coil never spans two spools** and one spool reference per output coil is correct *by design*. And `' FL1 … 2. Ensure FL2 can ALWAYS create valid stops` — implemented as `VALIDATE FINAL STOP POSSIBILITY` and `PREVENT INVALID FINAL REMAINDER`, i.e. **FL1 sizing is already constrained by FL2's ability to make shippable coils**, which is the inversion proposed on the 20 Aug call and built three months earlier.<br><br>**Findings that settle open questions.** The stop suffix is a **per-spool stop index shared by every alpha part in that stop** — which explains `R00004AB` existing with no `R00004AA` as *correct*, and means alpha + suffix is **not a unique key**. **LIFO is deliberate code** (`For revIndex = alphaPartCount To 1 Step -1`), so the tool treats *last on, first off* as fact — evidence for `Q45`, though a tool is not a client statement. `efficiency = totalOutput / (rodsUsed × rodWeight)` is a **working definition of metallic yield**, which `OI-60` / `Q11` lack. And the **400 lb overproduction discussed on the call is the anti-remainder rule working as intended** — 40,000 ÷ 1,800 leaves 400 lb, `400 < stopMin`, so the last spool is raised to 800 and the run totals 40,400.<br><br>⚠ **Three defects, two of them latent — do not port them.** (1) `PREVENT INVALID FINAL REMAINDER` **can emit a coil above the customer maximum** to avoid an unshippable tail; latent only because 1,800 divides cleanly by 900. (2) The FL1 sizing loop subtracts `targetSpoolWeight` rather than the `proposedSpool` it just allocated, so its accounting drifts whenever the validate step raises a spool; masked for the same reason. (3) `rodsUsed` is recomputed from output weight instead of counted from the segments the loop already built — benign here, two sources of truth in general.<br><br>⚠ **The workbook's rod weight is 4,000 lb** (`INPUT!C3`) — a **third** figure beside the transcript's ~5,500 lb and the contracts' 8,690–8,840 lb (**`OI-97`**, open). An input cell, so a data variance rather than a defect, but every count in the run depends on it. **Nothing in this document is citable as a requirement.** |

Its `coils` reference **does not resolve in CommonDB in the scripted schema** — a deployment-verification item now gating FL1 as well as Phase 9. Its no-locks design is **structural**: twelve objects across four databases cannot be locked without MSDTC. Suffix exhaustion is a **silent infinite loop**. The caller's *“sixteen tables”* is 14 selects over 12 objects, stated twice. Separately, **`CoilTraceability`'s header justifies its design on a case that cannot happen** — a coil spanning two spools, when welding is FL1-only and `Q17` made FL2 check-in exclusive; the design is right for a different reason (many *rods*, one spool) and the rationale needs correcting. And **`SpoolOrder` loses the order boundary** (no positional columns) while its stated derivation documents a workaround written *because this document's table did not exist* — both free to fix only while nothing writes it. |

Footages are rounded to 10 ft and **made to sum exactly within every container**; verified by recomputation, along with half-open range contiguity at all three hops and every enumerated value against its live `CHECK` list. ⚠ The 4,000 lb rod is one of three figures in circulation (`OI-97` / `OQ-J`) and every count scales with it. ## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Database/Schema/SQL/FlatWire_SampleData_Schedule.sql](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Database/Schema/SQL/FlatWire_SampleData_Schedule.sql)

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | August 27, 2026 | **Reissued for client review, and one live data defect fixed.** ⚠ **The eleven `Description` literals contained `→`, `×` and `—`.** SQLCMD reads an input file under the ANSI code page unless told otherwise, and U+2192 has no CP1252 representation, so every description was being **inserted corrupted** — the dev `FlatWireDB` seeded on 23 Aug holds `1100 rod ?+' 0.110" A- 0.500" round edge ??" FL1 standalone`. All eleven are now `->` / `x` / `-`, and **the whole file is ASCII-only with CRLF endings**, so no code page can corrupt it again. **No data value changed** — verified by diffing every `VALUES` tuple against the previous revision: the 11 descriptions are the only difference. **Two comment defects corrected:** the component block for `PS-1100-FL2-001` was headed *"Hybrid · Active"* against an `Inactive` header row, and the `PS-6061-FL1-001` block claimed a first-pass reduction of *18.3%* where 0.375″→0.340″ is **17.8%**. **Added:** `PRINT` confirmations and skip messages on all three blocks, matching the lookup seed's house style (this script had none); a **verification block** that reports the three row counts and the schedule mix, so a client can confirm the load; and a **seven-item OPEN POINTS block**. Open point 1 is the substantive one — **several fixtures draw harder per pass than the provisional per-alloy limits seeded in `AlloyProperty`**, which is consistent with `FR-383`/`OI-93` holding that the authoritative limit is `united_db..alloys.Draw_max_reduction`, per-pass-versus-cumulative unconfirmed; the die selections will be re-worked once that is answered. **Internal citations removed** (`D-31`, `G40`, `G41`, `FR-091`, the `TrialRunPlan.md §8` pointer, the *"this tally read 4/7 until now"* note); the trial-fixture and demotion rationale is kept, in business language. Verified by a clean load on a throwaway database — 11 / 77 / 3 rows, the coverage matrix reproduced exactly from the loaded data, the filtered unique index satisfied, and a re-run skipping all three blocks |

A failed bundle is already on the payoff, so writing no row reported an occupied bay as free. **Q72 item 3 — what *releases* a blocked row — is the blocking residual**: `Status` has no value for a WIP-rejection outcome, and a fourth value would move the row outside `UX_RodStaging_Bay`'s filter and free a bay that is not free. From the Dashboard 2A UX review finding F2 (`Analysis/Dashboard2A_UXReview.md`, deleted 1 Aug 2026 — in git history at `2a0426b`). |
| July 29, 2026 | **Free rod processing order.** Planned sequence is not enforced — staging validates only current-order membership and availability. Added `CK_RodStaging_SeqPos` / `CK_RodStaging_PlannedSeqPos`; deliberately **no** constraint relating the two, since a difference is the normal case. Also annotated that `PCI008`'s "enforce sequencing" means *physical weld* sequencing, not planned order (**Q70** partly resolved). |
| July 29, 2026 | Documented that the Dashboard 2A / `GET /payoff/status` **`Blocked`** bay state is **derived** (`Status = 'Staged'` + any inspection column `= 'Fail'`), not a fourth `Status` value — adding one would fall outside the `UX_RodStaging_Bay` filter and free a bay that is still physically occupied. ## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/BusinessRules.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/BusinessRules.md)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 22, 2026 | **First entry for this document, and §3.3a added — rod ↔ order cardinality and the four-tier sequence it forces.** States the full cardinality (rod→many orders, spool→many rods, spool→many orders, FL2 output exactly one order at a time), that orders are consumed one at a time per **rod payoff station** — FL1/FL3, FL2's equivalent being a separate rule — and that a shared rod is **position-locked**: last of the outgoing order, first of the incoming one. The partition is **pinned-first → free full → free partial → pinned-last**, so the legal sequence count is `|free full|! × |free partial|!`. **Two traps are called out:** a rod may be pinned at **both** ends — an order lying wholly inside one rod — so the end tiers are not necessarily different rods; and `Q73`'s *“multi-order coils last”* and the *“last rod of the outgoing order”* rule are **the same statement** read from opposite sides, so reading `Q73` alone makes the pinned-**first** case look like a violation of it |

## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/ProcessFlows.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/ProcessFlows.md)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 22, 2026 | **First entry for this document, and §4.4a added — the order boundary as a handoff inside one mount.** The one flow in which an operator action closes one order and starts the next **with no material movement at all**: rod checked in once → allocation reached, detected **server-side** on the footage stream → durable notification → **the line keeps running** → operator marks complete → next order on the same rod, same run. Carries the trigger-and-writes table, including that the weight is **latched twice** — at the crossing and at the acknowledgement — because the difference is the overrun and it must be recorded rather than discarded. **Three consequences that surprise people are stated outright:** one run spans both orders (the schema forces it — a run is one row per check-in event and a check-in points at exactly one run), the PLC tags are pushed **once**, and **FL1 does not wait for FL2** — an order is *consumed* at FL1 and *produced* at FL2, and is complete only when both are true |

## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Backend/tasks/FW-080.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Backend/tasks/FW-080.md)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 15, 2026 | **First issue — the build order for `FW-080`, the one RT-stream story in this set.** Records two decisions. **`P-21`:** the MessagePack package is **named in no specification** — `[SIG §4.1]` prescribes `AddSignalR().AddMessagePackProtocol()` without saying what supplies it, and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack` is absent from `API/Directory.Packages.props`, where central package management requires it to be added. | August 15, 2026 | **First issue.** Records that this story is what makes `[SVC §3.2]`'s hardest rule survivable — Application may not reference SignalR types, which leaves a command handler no way to broadcast its own side effect, and **the tempting fix is to inject `IHubContext`**. Domain events are the answer the specification already chose, *"satisfied rather than worked around."* **`P-34`** makes the negative acceptance criterion structural instead of disciplinary: `FlatWire.Application`'s `.csproj` carries **no** SignalR package reference and no reference to the API project, so a handler reaching for `IHubContext` **fails to compile** — a stronger guarantee than a review note, costing nothing, and matching how `FW-205` `P-25` enforces its own absence. **`P-35`** puts the translation handlers in **Infrastructure**, where `[SVC §3.2c]` leaves the choice open: they are dispatched by `FlatWireDbContext`, the API project is already the composition root, and a domain-event-to-hub translation is not a business rule. Records the two rules most likely to be violated quietly: **dispatch after `SaveChangesAsync`, never before** — dispatching first broadcasts a state the database may still reject — and **`WipRejection` clears a blocked bay by publishing, not by reaching into `RodStaging`**, which is shorter and works and breaks the aggregate boundary, `Blocked` being a **derived** condition rather than a field to clear. Also notes the dispatcher is inherited but **not reusable**: `MediatorExtension.DispatchDomainEventsAsync` is strongly typed to the concrete context and must be recreated against `FlatWireDbContext`. |
| August 27, 2026 | ⚠ **Reviewed against the built code, and the card's central instruction was wrong. `P-94`–`P-96` minted.** ⛔ **The finding that reframes the story: nothing dispatches at all.** `SaveEntitiesAsync` is the only method that calls the dispatcher and **no caller anywhere invokes it**; `SaveChangesAsync` is **not overridden**; and `TransactionBehaviour` wraps every command and commits through `CommitTransactionAsync`, which calls that plain `SaveChangesAsync`. **So every one of the six events `FW-207` raises is collected on the entity and thrown away.** Build step 1 could not catch it because it checked the wrong method — and worse, it instructed the developer to confirm `SaveEntitiesAsync` dispatches *after* `SaveChangesAsync`, **a reorder the context's own remarks forbid**, which would have moved the in-transaction handlers out of the transaction (`P-95`).<br><br>⛔ **AC 2 is wrong twice over** — the dispatching method is `SaveEntitiesAsync`, and it drains **before** the save *deliberately* so handlers sharing the scoped context enlist in the same transaction. `FW-142` wrote that in terms: *"`FW-208` owns POST-COMMIT dispatch … do not reorder this method — `FW-208` adds a second, post-commit path."* ⛔ **And that second path cannot be a second call**: the inherited dispatcher runs `ClearDomainEvents()` **before** its publish loop, so a post-commit re-scan finds an empty change tracker and publishes nothing, silently. `P-94` makes it **capture-then-replay across two lanes** — database-writing handlers in-transaction (post-commit, a crash between commit and handler leaves a bay blocked forever), broadcasts after `CommitAsync()` (in-transaction, a rollback has already told nine operators a lie) — with three required properties: a rollback publishes nothing, the buffer clears before an execution-strategy retry, and a post-commit handler touches no tracked entity. **This makes the story a mechanism to design, contradicting its own *"not a mechanism to design"* premise**; hours owed to the re-baseline, no cell restated.<br><br>**`P-96` assigns every event a lane in writing, and two events get both** — `BayStateChanged` (release the bay in-transaction, broadcast after) and `WeldRecorded` (mark the rod welded in-transaction, only when `QualityPassed` per `WLD010`). §2.2 had **one** handler doing both, which is incorrect on either lane. **Six other corrections:** the events are **six, not five** (`FW-207` added `RunResumed`); **AC 1 and build steps 2–3 are already delivered** by `FW-207`; **§2.3's *"must be recreated"* is done** (`FW-142` built `FlatWire.Infrastructure/MediatorExtension.cs`); ⛔ **AC 3 is not buildable** — `IFlatWireClient` and `FlatWireHub` exist in **no** `ual-api` checkout, so the handler half is blocked on `FW-080` (`P-22`) while steps 1a–6 are not; ✅ **`G38` is closed** by `FW-207`, which persists the prompt to `FlatWireRun`'s five columns, so a missed broadcast is recovered by a refresh; and the card's *"No stale citations in this card"* is **struck** — there were six, now tabulated. `P-34` re-verified as still true: `Application.csproj` references only `Domain.csproj` and carries no SignalR package. |
| August 27, 2026 | ⚠ **Re-reviewed before execution, and the mechanism the earlier review specified was NOT IMPLEMENTABLE. `P-97` minted.** ⛔ `P-96` said the dispatch lane was *"decided by which dispatcher publishes it … key it off the handler's marker interface"*. **`mediator.Publish` invokes EVERY registered `INotificationHandler<TEvent>`** — MediatR 12.4.1 offers no per-call handler selection — so with both handlers subscribed to `BayStateChanged`, the drain would have run the **broadcast handler pre-commit**: the exact failure the two lanes were designed to prevent, reintroduced by the design meant to prevent it. `P-97` puts the lane in the notification **type** (`InTransaction<TEvent>` / `PostCommit<TEvent>`) so MediatR routes it and the compiler enforces it, with the run-time `MakeGenericType` confined to the dispatcher and its closed types cached. **Two alternatives are rejected on the record:** resolving and filtering handlers manually reimplements the part of MediatR that pipeline behaviours hook into, so `LoggingBehavior` would stop seeing domain-event handlers; and letting broadcast handlers self-defer into a flush queue is a **discipline rather than a guarantee** — a handler that sends directly gets a pre-commit broadcast and no compile error.<br><br>**Three further corrections to the same pass.** ⚠ **`SaveEntitiesAsync` cannot be deleted** — it is declared on `UA.Framework.Domain.Uow.IUnitOfWork`, so the earlier *"should not be left as an orphan"* was wrong about what is possible; route it through the same hook instead. ⚠ **The build order put classification AFTER the mechanism that depends on it** — the dispatcher cannot be written without knowing which events go on which lane, so lane assignment is now step 2 and the doubled `1. 1a` numbering is gone; the order is a flat 1–10, with the in-transaction handlers pulled forward to step 7 because they are **buildable now** and are the half whose loss leaves a bay blocked forever. ⚠ **`PayoffStateChanged` is a name for an unbuilt interface member** — confirm it against `FW-149` rather than inventing it here. `P-94` also gains two properties, now five: the buffer is a **local** so rollback-safety and retry-safety hold structurally, and the post-commit publish sits **outside the `try`** or a failing broadcast triggers `RollbackTransaction()` against an already-committed transaction. |

Delivered: the two lane wrappers `InTransaction<TEvent>`/`PostCommit<TEvent>` (`P-97`), capture-then-replay hooked into **`CommitTransactionAsync`** (`P-95`), `SaveEntitiesAsync` routed through the same hook so the two entry points cannot diverge, and the two **in-transaction** handlers — `BayReleaseHandler` and `WeldMarkHandler` — in `Infrastructure/EventHandlers/` per `P-35`. **Verified by harness on live `FlatWireDB`** (no endpoint reaches an aggregate): lane routing with the **raw event reaching neither lane**, both lanes dispatching **in-transaction then broadcast** asserted on sequence, the bay **actually released** — `Status='Unstaged'`, attributed to the rejection's operator — inside the rejection's own transaction, a failed commit **broadcasting nothing** with the write rolled back, and `WLD010` (a failed weld does not mark the rod; a redelivery does not overwrite the first stamp). `FW-207`'s 137 checks still pass and the API still boots. ⛔ **Step 8 remains blocked** — `IFlatWireClient` and `FlatWireHub` still exist in no checkout (`FW-080`, `P-22`).<br><br>⛔ **Three defects only execution could find, and all three were silent.** **(1) `INotificationHandler<>` was never registered.** The Scrutor scan covered the five *request* handler shapes and nothing else, and `AddCommonApplication()` was called with no extra assemblies, so a notification handler in Infrastructure would compile, look registered and never resolve — `Publish` finding zero handlers and **completing successfully having done nothing**. That is the **third** silent no-op in this story, after the missing hook and clear-before-publish. Both fixed. **(2) The in-transaction lane could not see a sibling aggregate's identity, so `P-94`'s order is REVISED to save → drain → save → commit.** `CK_RodStaging_RejectLink` requires `WipRejectionId` whenever `UnstageKind = 'WipRejection'`, and the rejection is inserted by the very command that raised the event — at drain time it is `Added` with `Id = 0`. Draining first made the link unknowable and the commit died on the CHECK constraint. Two saves, **one transaction**, atomicity unaffected. **(3) `BayStateChanged` had to be split — `P-98`.** The earlier review raised the overload as an open item saying a distinct event *"would remove the guards"*; execution proved it **required**: a notification raised by four other `RodStaging` call sites cannot carry a rejection link, so the release was unwritable. `BayReleaseRequested` carries the rejection's **business** key and the handler resolves the surrogate — which works only because of (2), so the handler throws a named exception rather than unstaging without the link.<br><br>⚠ **`FW-207`'s event surface was edited here**, for the same reason `FW-146`'s arm was edited by `FW-207`: the consumer is what proves the surface incomplete. `BayStateChanged` and `WeldRecorded` gained **`OperatorId`** (`Unstage` needs `unstagedBy`, `MarkWelded` needs `weldedBy`, and both DDL columns mean a person), and `RodStaging.ConsumeAtCheckIn` gained `checkedInBy`. **No hour cell restated** — the 8 h basis reads *"the dispatcher itself is inherited"*, true of the pre-commit drain and not of the post-commit lane; owed to the re-baseline. |
| August 29, 2026 | ✅ **STEP 8 EXECUTED — the five broadcast handlers, and the story is complete but for one event that has nowhere to go. `P-137`–`P-139` minted; `OI-140` raised.** `FW-080` landed `IFlatWireClient` in `FlatWire.Domain` on 28 Aug, so `P-35`'s placement holds and the handlers are in `FlatWire.Infrastructure/EventHandlers/`: `BayStateChangedBroadcastHandler` · `WeldRecordedBroadcastHandler` · `RunPausedBroadcastHandler` · `RunResumedBroadcastHandler` · `SpoolCompletionPromptBroadcastHandler`. **5 new files, 5 amended, 0 errors, 13 solution-wide warnings — the pre-existing baseline unchanged. Harness 54/54**, sections A–B in process and section C against live `FlatWireDB` (both lanes dispatching, `intx` before `send`, a failed transaction broadcasting nothing, and a throwing broadcast NOT failing the committed command). ⛔ **`P-137` — `CoilCompleted` gets no handler**: `[SIG §5.2]`'s fourteen events and `[SIG §5.4]`'s six markers carry **no coil-completion member**, and adding one is breaking under `[API §8]`; raised as **`OI-140`**. It is also the source of the *“eight broadcast handlers”* figure in `FW-080` / `FW-149` / `Orchestration.md`, which miscounts eight **handlers** (six post-commit + two in-transaction) as eight broadcasts — corrected at all three sites. ⛔ **`P-138` — the post-commit replay was UNGUARDED**, and `DispatchLanes.cs` documented a rule pointing at an enforcement that did not exist: the first throwing broadcast would have turned a **committed** command into a `500`. Guarded at the context in `PublishDeferredSafelyAsync`, which both entry points now route through; `FlatWireDbContext` gained `ILogger<FlatWireDbContext>` and the design factory passes `NullLogger`. ⚠ **`P-139` — three events could not fill their own payloads**: `WeldRecorded` gained `LineId` (without it there was no group to address, so the weld was **unbroadcastable**), `RunResumed` gained `FootageAtResume` (`PauseMarker.FootagePosition` is non-nullable), and `BayStateChanged` gained `RodSeqno` / `IsWelded` / `IsBlocked`. ## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Backend/tasks/FW-218.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Backend/tasks/FW-218.md)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 15, 2026 | **First issue — trial scope, additive to `[CE §3b]`.** The story exists because **the trial was specified to demonstrate behaviour it had no way to trigger** (`G43`): three of `[TRP §8]`'s ten steps need the feed **steered while a run is live**, and the only lever without a control surface is configuration plus a restart, **which destroys the run being demonstrated** — the very thing steps 7 and 10 assert about. **`P-38`** records why conditional route registration and a policy guard are not equivalent, though they look so in review: a mapped-but-forbidden route **exists**, is discoverable, and is protected only by correct role configuration, whereas an unregistered route cannot be reached by any caller in any role — hence `[SIM §2.4]`'s absolute, **`404`, not `403`**, with `Engineer`/`Admin` layered on top and **never `Operator`**. **`P-39`** requires the four endpoints to carry the **paths, shapes and semantics `[SIM §8.1]` already specifies**, implemented over `FW-203` instead of the line model, so `FW-215` later **extends** rather than replaces and `FW-214`'s greyed controls light up as configuration — *"do not invent a simpler shape because only four endpoints are in scope."* Records that these are **not among `[API]`'s endpoints** and must not be added to the 32-row count. ⚠ **§7.1 reports that `FW-218` appears nowhere in `phase-01b`** — zero occurrences, though it has a full card in `[TB §7]` (Critical, S1, Phase 1B, Stream BE) and a row in `[TRP §1.4]`. **Reported, not fixed**: adding it changes an hours-bearing document, and `[TRP §1.4]`'s arithmetic already carries it (BE 145 → 156, total 220 → 231). |
| August 29, 2026 | ✅ **BUILT, and `P-38` VERIFIED BOTH WAYS — `G43` is resolved.** Four endpoints at `/sim` (`POST {line}/steer`, `DELETE {line}/run`, `POST {line}/fault`, `GET /state`) over `FW-203`'s levers, 0 errors and no new analyzer warning. **Measured, both directions:** simulation **OFF** → `/sim/state`, `/sim/{line}/steer` and `/sim/{line}/fault` all return **404** and the real ingest registers in their place, failing loudly by name on `G60` exactly as `FW-N05` designed; simulation **ON** → `/sim/state` returns **401** and a `GET` on the steer route **405**, so the routes exist and are auth-gated. ⛔ **`P-136`, and it is two choices `P-38` implies without stating.** **(1) A minimal-API GROUP rather than a controller**, so *“not registered at all”* is literal: an attribute-routed controller is discovered by the MVC application model and would have to be removed by a convention — the route exists and is then un-mapped, which is the weaker claim `P-38` exists to reject. It is mapped inside the same `if` that chooses the publisher, so the control plane and the thing it controls can never disagree about whether the feed is synthetic. **(2) The role layer FAILS CLOSED.** `[SIM §8.4]` requires Engineer or Admin and never Operator, but **`FW-145` is unbuilt, issues no role claim, and these routes therefore deny everyone today.** The alternative — a bare `[Authorize]` — would have let the trial run immediately and shipped *“any authenticated operator may drive the control plane”*, the one thing that section forbids. ⚠ **A control surface that is too permissive is invisible; one that is too strict announces itself on the first call**, so **`FW-145` is now a recorded hard dependency for the acceptance run** rather than a discovery on the day. ⚠ **`POST /sim/{lineId}/run` stays out** per the card, so a line stopped through `DELETE .../run` stays stopped until the service restarts — acceptable because the stop is the acceptance run's last assertion, and the fifth endpoint arrives with `FW-215`. **Nothing added to `[API §3.2]`'s 32 rows** — `/sim` is outside `/api/v1/flatwire` by design. **No hours, scope or acceptance criteria changed.** |

with a measurement. ⛔ **Execution found a defect three reviews did not: the configuration binder APPENDS to a collection that already holds C# defaults.** `IngestLines = ["FL1","FL2"]` in code plus the same two in `appsettings` bound to **`FL1, FL2, FL1, FL2`** — four poll loops reading every tag **twice a second** — and the boot log printed it: *"OPC ingest started: FL1, FL2, FL1, FL2."* **The worse half is not the doubling:** a deployer setting `["FL3"]` would have got `FL1, FL2, FL3` and **could not remove the first two**, so the `{FL1,FL2}`-or-`{FL3}` rule this card had just established to stop FL3 double-reading FL2's namespace would have been unhonourable from configuration. Fixed by removing the C# default (**`P-123`** — the default lives in `appsettings.json`, where it can be overridden, and the validator refuses an empty list by name) plus a **dedupe guard** in the service, since a deployer listing a line twice is the same defect by hand. ⚠ Scoped to bound **lists**: `Tags`/`LineStateMap` are dictionaries and `Confirmed` is a set, so `FW-144`'s options were never affected. ✅ **Re-booted clean: `FL1, FL2` once each.** ✅ **`G59` and `G60` reproduced by boot, by name.** With the flag flipped both lines log *"cannot resolve … `FlatWireOpc:OpcModuleId` is not configured (gap G60 …)"* — **once per line, two lines in 15 seconds of ticking** — and **the host stayed up**: health `200`, `database.reachable: true`. That last property is the one that matters and it was designed for: an unhandled exception in a `BackgroundService` stops the host by default, and this service is *expected* to fail until `G59`/`G60` are settled, so every loop catches, logs and continues. **A deferred, blocked ingest does not take the API down.** ⚠ **Two of this card's own numbers are corrected by the build.** The read list is **14 of FL1's 17 paths and 11 of FL2's 22 — 25 tag reads in 2 POSTs a second**, not the ~37 estimated, because a read needs somewhere to land: the write-only interlock, the two derived edger keys (`ComponentName` carries **one** `EdgeSet` member for FM2's **two** edgers) and the ten dancer elements are excluded, each logged at boot with its reason (**`P-122`**, a partial answer to `G31` rather than a closure). ⚠ **And one is now stale: `Polly` IS in `FlatWire.Infrastructure`'s package set** — `FW-151` added it the same day. What was actually missing was **`Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions`**, which AC 1's placement requires and which was **not** centrally pinned; added at **8.0.1** to match the net8.0 shared framework (**`P-121`**, `P-108`'s case and not `P-101`'s — an ordinary NuGet package, so no Domain-side indirection). ⚠ **One review finding withdrawn on contact with the code:** the *"no fault tag on any FM2 stand"* item is **already tracked** — `TagNames.Fm2S3Faulted` carries a derived path and its own note citing `PLC-Q02` / `[PLC §5.4]`. The observation was right; it was not new, and no gap needed minting. ⚠ **`TC-620`–`TC-623` stay untestable** (`G9`/`OI-34`): the harness proves the channel *behaves*, not that 1024 is *right*. The harness is **scratchpad-only and deliberately not in the repository** — `[TS §1.2]` withdraws automated backend tests, and adding a test project would reverse that decision from inside a leaf story; §5 records how to reproduce it in four assertions. |

The change is one of **shape**: **+640 px of width (×1.50) against +56 px of height (×1.05)**, and **5:4 → 16:9**, so **the re-layout is horizontal and nothing gets taller** — which is why the sub-14 px chart-axis exception on `dashboard_3_active_run` / `_fl2` / `_fl3` is now stated to **survive** the change rather than being relieved by it: its reason is vertical, and the canvas gained 56 px, one row of 14 px type with padding. ⚠ **The 14 px floor and ≥ 48 px tap targets are carried forward on a stated, unconfirmed assumption** — both are *physical* legibility rules (arm's length, standing, gloved), so they track **dpi, not resolution**, and they hold only if the new panel is **physically larger** of the same dpi class (~21.5″ 16:9 against a 17–19″ 5:4, both ~96–102 dpi). **If it is the same panel at higher density, every size scales ×1.5 and the floor becomes 21 px** — a change to the token system, not to the layouts. **No document records the panel's diagonal**: `G23` and `Q26` asked about resolution only, so the section now asks for it. The 14 px figure's authority also moved: it was cited as *"`MIN_FONT` in `flat-wire-fit.js`"*, a **mockup** asset that hard-codes the old design box and has no Angular equivalent, so the number is this table's and the script is merely where the mockups implement it. ⛔ **The Print row was wrong and four `Must` requirements contradicted it** — it read *"**no print action** on any operator screen"*, against `FR-336` (*"a coil label preview shall be shown before printing"*), `FR-146` (labels print once the spool-completion transaction commits), `FR-335` (closing a skid prints the skid label) and `FR-340` (FL1 and FL2 each equipped with two label printers). The rule is *no **traveler** printing*; as written, a developer building DB7 from this document would omit the print control and QA would test for its absence — and those two are exactly its stated audience. **Added:** a **Dialog height** row (*no dialog scrolls; an oversized dialog is scaled to fit*), which was documented only in `CLAUDE.md` and owned by no specification; a note naming the **four constraints the repository already satisfies** — `ngx-touch-keyboard` and `shared`'s `KeypadComponent` for data entry, and `CommonPopupService`'s `backdrop: 'static'` + `keyboard: false` for both modal rows, which satisfies them **by construction** and whose failure mode is using `NgbModal` directly; and **§7.5a**, which records that the **client-side validation this document's title and Document Type both claim has never been written**, naming the four things with no home — `FW-131`'s toast-versus-inline rules, `FW-134`'s `.input` states, the field formats `FW-132` bakes into its models, and **`G14`'s two unresolved halves** (3- versus 4-item inspection, `FootageFt` INT versus DECIMAL). |

## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Architecture/MachineSimulator.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Architecture/MachineSimulator.md)

| Date | Changed By | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Aug 15, 2026 | Plan team | **First issue, `[SIM]`.** Specifies the FL1/FL2/FL3 machine simulator and its engineering console `DB-S1`. Eleven sections: the four rules (§2), the seam and two adapters (§3), the three line models (§4), the kinematic model and its **A1–A10 assumption table** (§5), the closed loop with `SimulatePLCTagPush` (§6), the scenario and fault catalogue (§7), the control surface (§8), the console (§9), what it cannot prove (§10), and open items (§11).<br><br>**Four things in it will look like defects to a reader who does not know they are deliberate.** **(1) It carries no PLC tag path strings and never may** — the same rule `[PLCC]` observes; `[PLC]` is the only tag map in the repository, and writing a path here would create the seventh copy. **(2) `FL2` ticks.** §4.2 states that only the *batched* `GaugeReading`/`WidthReading` are suppressed — `SpeedFPM`, `FootageCounter`, `PayoffWeight`, `ComponentStatus` and `LineStatus` still flow, and gauge is still computed internally for the `RunReading` profile. A simulator treating FL2 as silent leaves both FL2 trial screens dead. **(3) Run status and line state are two vocabularies** (§4.4): `CK_FlatWireRun_Status` is ours and settled; the line-state vocabulary is ours and **unconfirmed** (`OI-35`). A mill can stop with the run still `Running`, and `FR-141`'s `RUNNING → STOPPED` edge is the *line* state. **(4) Mill spring places the roll gap *below* gauge**, load-proportionally (§5.5) — springback-as-an-alloy-multiplier putting the gap above gauge is the error master spec §10.5 exists to correct, a machine stiffness misfiled as a material property.<br><br>**§5.6 is the document's load-bearing table.** Ten assumptions, each naming its basis and the commissioning test that confirms it. **A8 and A9 are permanent simplifications** (lateral spread and rolling force are not modelled, against `PSG` §3.3.3 and §3.3.6); **A1–A7 are provisional and must be reconciled**. It is gap **`G39`**'s only instrument, and the act that closes it — commissioning step **`C13`** — is **not yet written into `[COM]`**.<br><br>Also records, in §1.4, that **there is no prior art in the UAL ecosystem** — `slitter-setup-simulator` is a slitting-pattern optimizer and `OPCConnection` has no simulation support — so the search is not repeated. |

| Aug 13, 2026 | **`build_development_plan_xlsx.py` documented — the fourth script, and the second client workbook builder.** Adds a summary-table row and a full section: what it reads, the seven sheets, the two-source construction, its guards, and the two figures it deliberately withholds. **Three notes are load-bearing.** *(1)* **`Reference title` is a mirror of the plan's own title, not authored prose** — paraphrasing it leaves the drift guard checking nothing, which is exactly what happened on the first build: 60 of 107 entries had hand-typed approximations and the guard rejected every one. *(2)* The two workbook builders **share their helpers by duplication, not import**, so a change to one deliverable's guard cannot silently change the other's. *(3)* Bare `Angular`, `.NET` and `SQL` are **not** blocked by the leakage guard — they name the technology, which the client already knows. Also corrected a stale link label left by the 13 Aug consolidation: the `ClientQuestionsContent.md` reference read `../../RequirementDocuments/…` against a target that is local to this folder. |
| Aug 12, 2026 | **`build_questions_xlsx.py` — Excel no longer repairs the workbook on open, and `Recommended answer` became optional.** Two changes, one a real defect. **(1) The repair.** Excel had been reporting *"Repaired Records: String properties from /xl/worksheets/sheet2.xml"* on every open — four repair logs in `%TEMP%` on 12 Aug alone — and the cause was a **whitespace-only rich-text run**. `render()` splits authored `**bold**` into runs, so two bold spans separated by a single space emit a run containing just `" "`; **openpyxl 3.1.5 writes `xml:space="preserve"` on a whitespace-*edged* run (`" x "`) but omits it on a whitespace-*only* one**, so XML normalisation strips the content and Excel sees an invalid run. Reproduced in isolation against openpyxl directly, so it is an upstream bug, not a data problem. Fixed in our code by `_fold_blank_runs()`, which **never emits such a run** — the whitespace is folded into an adjacent run instead of dropped, so the text is byte-identical (a bold space renders the same as a plain one). The single offending cell was `D27`, the `Q83` die-life decision. Verified by opening the rebuilt workbook through Excel COM: **no new repair log**. The defect was independent of any content change and had been shipping in the client deliverable. **(2)** `Recommended answer` moved from `REQUIRED_OPEN` to the optional set beside `Options` and `Already agreed`, because `Q19` (footage-to-weight) deliberately carries no recommendation; `build()` was also switched to `.get()` for that field, a missing required field having previously been guaranteed by the guard, and the Open Questions caption relaxed from *"each with our recommended answer"* to *"almost all with"*. |

They are now **drawn as boxes and lines** out of table cells (see above). Also: **HTML comments are stripped**, since `<!-- TOC -->` was rendering as a literal paragraph on the first page; and the script now **refuses to render onto `MVP-2/SRS/PassScheduleGenerationSpec.docx`**, which is its own branding template — `shutil.copyfile` raises `SameFileError` on that path, so rebuilding *that* file means rendering to a temp path and moving it into place. |

| Aug 13, 2026 | Plan team | **Created — the development plan as a client deliverable.** Seven sheets to `MVP-1/SRS/FlatWire_DevelopmentPlan.xlsx`: *Read Me · Delivery Options · Plan by Stage · Sprint Schedule · Work Items · Milestones and Needs · Assumptions and Risks*. Built to the same two-source shape as `build_questions_xlsx.py` — **structure parsed, prose authored** — with `DevelopmentPlanContent.md` as the only home of the client wording and `TaskBreakdown.md` / `StaffedSprintPlans.md` supplying every figure, so a plan change propagates on the next run rather than being retyped.<br><br>**The prose had to be written, not filtered, and the count is why: 68 of the 116 work-item titles trip the leakage guard** — 40 carry code spans, 11 name endpoints, 10 use screen numbers, 7 name database tables. Deleting those does not leave a sentence. The raw material is each story's `So that` clause, **only 4 of which trip the guard**; they were already client language, and every *Delivers* line is built from one. Seeded mechanically from the `As a / I want / So that` triads, then hand-edited — the seeds were a starting point, not the deliverable.<br><br>**Two presentation rules are enforced in code rather than trusted to the author.** Effort is converted to **days** at write time and hours never appear — hours invite a rate conversation. The **unit rate card is never exported**: per-stage and per-item totals are fine, *what a screen costs* is internal pricing mechanics. A small `plain()` pass rewrites internal shorthand in *parsed commentary only* (`Q4` → *the fourth quarter*), never in a figure.<br><br>**Four fatal guards**, coverage and drift keyed on the plan's work items and phases. `LEAKS` gains two patterns over the questions workbook — **library names** and **code identifiers** (anything ending `Service`, `Controller`, `Repository`, `Component`, `Hub`, `Dto`, `Handler`) — chosen because they are what survives a careless content edit. **Verified by deliberate breach**, twice: a repository path, a requirement id, a backlog id, an endpoint, a service name, a library name and a table name were injected into content fields; all seven were named with sheet and cell coordinates, the workbook was deleted and the build exited 1.<br><br>**Three defects found and fixed during verification, all of the same class — parsed structure taken at face value.** The staffed-plan tables carry a **totals row with no sprint label**, which was being counted as a sprint and made the schedule sheet contradict its own headline (11/8/6 sprints against 10/7/5); it is now detected and labelled *Total*. Sprint dates carry **the year on the closing row only**, which is fine read top to bottom and wrong on a milestone sheet where *08 Jan* stands alone and is not 2026; the year is recovered by rolling over when the month goes backwards. And **60 of 107 `Reference title` fields were hand-typed paraphrases**, which the drift guard rejected outright — they are now synced verbatim from the plan, since a paraphrased mirror checks nothing. |

The Sprint Plan subtitle likewise moved from *“Four sprints from 17 August”* to *“Four blocks of work from 31 August”*.<br><br>**One parser anchor was brittle and is now keyed on identity rather than wording**: `_rows_after(text, '### 2.1 Recommended shape', …)` matched the heading's *prose*, so retitling §2.1 for the three-resource shape failed the build outright with *“heading not found”*. Anchored on **`'### 2.1'`**. | Aug 14, 2026 | Plan team | **Created** — the trial-run workbook builder, writing ten sheets from `[TRP]` + `[TB]` + `TrialRunContent.md`. **61 work items, 778 hours**, every figure parsed rather than typed.<br><br>**Three parser problems worth recording, because each is the kind of thing that returns.** A helper that found *"the first table under a heading"* could not address the plan's sections that carry **two or three tables before their first sub-heading** — §1.3 alone has three — so it was rewritten to return the **nth** table, bounded by heading depth, with an `expect` assertion matched against the **whole header row** rather than the first cell, since several of the plan's tables deliberately leave the first column heading blank. **Footer rows are the second trap and they cut both ways**: the block table's footer restates the grand total and must be dropped or the sum double-counts to 1,556; the three-bases footer carries the totals the guards check and must be kept — dropping it made `1C` look like the total and raised a bare `StopIteration`. Both are now filtered on a *data* condition rather than on a blank first cell. Third, the plan's **final sprint carries em dashes** for capacity and utilisation because it is testing and sign-off with no development hours — a deliberate dash is not a parse failure and now defaults to zero.<br><br>**The expander and the guard must agree on their word boundary, and for one build they did not.** The expander used `[\w-]`, the guard `\b`, so a hyphen-joined compound like `DB3-FL2` was **flagged but never expanded** — an unfixable failure from the user's side. The expander now uses `\w`, matching the guard. Code identifiers stay safe because they join on word characters and underscores, never hyphens: `PLCTagService`, `FlatWireDbContext` and `sp_GetGaugeTrace` are all untouched, and no hyphen-delimited segment of `run-status-cards` or `chart-tab-strip` is an abbreviation. |

## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/build_allocation_examples_xlsx.py](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/build_allocation_examples_xlsx.py)

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| August 24, 2026 | **First issue.** The rod-to-order worked-example workbook — `MVP-1/SRS/FlatWire_OrderAllocationExamples.xlsx`, thirteen sheets, 24 rules, 60 worked examples. The repository's **eighth** script and **fourth** workbook builder, duplicating its helpers per the standing rule. Sheets: *Read Me · The Rules · Worked Examples · One Rod, One Order · Two Rods, One Spool · Order Handoff · Processing Order Options · Weight and Footage · Order Completion · Full Planned Run · Heavier Rod Run · Orders Across the Run · What We Need Confirmed*.<br><br>**Why it exists.** `RodOrderAllocation.md` states outright that the sequence tiers, the handoff state machine and the fulfilment rollup are *“our reading of the client rules, not client-confirmed text”*, and `Q48` is `Critical` and open. Twenty requirements and twenty-one test cases were written against that reading with **nothing the client could read back**. Every rule now appears in plain language with an accept case and a refuse case, and the client's own planner run is reproduced end to end.<br><br>**It is the first generator whose figures are computed rather than parsed**, and the arithmetic guard is what makes that safer than transcribing rather than riskier. It re-derives the conversion (`A = t·w` square, `A = t·w − 0.2146·t²` round, `k = 12ρ`), the four-tier sequence validator and the client planner including `VALIDATE FINAL STOP POSSIBILITY`, then checks all three against figures published independently: **all twenty conversion cells in `[DBD §6.6]`**, the three worked footage figures in the design document, and the planner's own published **11 rods · 23 spools · 45 stops · 40,400 lb · 91.82 % · 9 welded spools** — all six of which the corrected port reproduces exactly.<br><br>⚠ **The three defects `FL Alphas Plus - Analysis.md` §6 says not to port are corrected, and correcting them is free on the shipped inputs** — 1,800 mod 900 = 0 leaves two of them latent and the rod count agrees at 11 — which is precisely why the corrected port still matches the published totals. A port that reproduced the defects would agree too, and would be wrong for any other input.<br><br>**Five guards, all fatal, every one proved by breaking it deliberately**: arithmetic, coverage (each rule has an accept and a non-accept example; all twenty-four enumeration values, eight state transitions and five order statuses appear somewhere), drift, team names, leakage. Plus **two warnings that are deliberately not fatal**, on the trial-run builder's reasoning that a guard refusing to build a document for saying something uncomfortable just gets switched off.<br><br>⚠ **The leakage guard was extended, and the extension is the finding.** The copied list was written before `RodOrderAllocation` and `RodOrderConsumption` existed, so it reported *“clean”* on the two table names this workbook is most likely to leak. Also added: the internal rule-code pattern, the `DF_`/`PK_`/`UQ_` constraint prefixes, and eight further table names. **Three source strings could not be used at all** because they trip the guard: the seeded order numbers and the local coil alpha both match the backlog-identifier pattern, and are replaced by the six-digit order number and the shared coil alpha — both forms already documented elsewhere, and both the ones the client actually uses.<br><br>⚠ **A one-unit rounding tolerance was found to be wide enough to hide a formula error, and was closed two ways.** Perturbing the round-edge constant from `0.2146` to `0.2100` moved five of the twenty cells by exactly one unit each and passed as five rounding warnings. The constant is now asserted directly against `1 − π/4`, and the **count** of cells needing the tolerance is asserted at exactly one — alloy 5052, round edge, drawing-line gauge, where `[DBD §6.6]` rounds `0.077082` down to `0.0770` against the formula's `0.0771`. That single cell is the only rounding disagreement in the published table. |

## [MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/build_coverage_matrix.py](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/build_coverage_matrix.py)

| Date | Changed By | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Aug 13, 2026 | Gap remediation | **Created — requirement coverage is now measured, not asserted.** Parses the requirement rows of `02-SRS.md` and the case rows of `06-TestPlanAndTestCases.md` and **exits non-zero** if any MVP-1 requirement has neither a test case nor a §10.4 entry. Written to the same shape as the coverage guard in `build_questions_xlsx.py`. Three precedence levels count as covered — **direct** (a §5 case names the requirement in its *FR / Source* column, that column and not the whole row), **indirect** (the SRS `NFR` table names both the requirement and a `TC-###`), **declared** (§10.4 records it with a reason) — on the principle that *a declared hole is a decision and an undeclared one is an accident*, and only the second fails the build. Withdrawn requirements (`~~**FR-###**~~`, four of them) are excluded; **`FR-111` is one, and counting it is how a false positive enters**. Carries an explicit non-goal: `05-SprintPlanAndBacklog.md` §11 has the same range granularity but **no per-requirement data to check against**, so its story assignments are reported as an advisory count that never affects exit status. |

What changed is that each dialog now receives its material context from the caller instead of hard-coding one run, which is what finally lets the pre-check-in rejection path (Q36 item 3) be represented: no run, no footage position, and submitting releases the bay. Two hand-offs the spec already described also become real — a gauge-drift or size-change die change opens the SPC checkpoint it mandates, and an out-of-spec checkpoint's *suspend material* opens the WIP rejection with the failing reading carried over. New open item **Q43**: DB1's "WIP Rejection**s**" nav item reads as a list screen that has never been specified. |

| Aug 13, 2026 | Gap remediation | **Coverage was asserted from a range table; 41 requirements had no test case.** §10.1 mapped SRS **section ranges** to TC ranges (`FR-100 – FR-120 → TC-130 – TC-147`) and the published **96.7 %** was concluded from that mapping — which cannot show that an *individual* requirement was tested, and therefore could not fail. Measured per requirement for the first time: **41 MVP-1 requirements are named by no case, 32 of them `Must`**. §10.2 (*every case names its requirement*) was true, machine-verified, and **the opposite direction** — a suite can name a requirement on every case and still leave requirements untested. **The denominator was wrong too:** **363** was the pre-split MVP-1 + MVP-2 total where `02-SRS.md` now carries **263**, §5.10/§5.18/§5.19/§5.23/§5.24 having left on 11 Aug 2026. Changes: §10.1 is **demoted to a navigation aid** and its five MVP-2 rows struck; §10.4 is split into **10.4.1 knowingly excluded** (a decision, with an owner) and **new 10.4.2**, itemising all 41 with what closes each — including the two that need only a citation added to an existing case (`FR-300` on `TC-377`, `FR-226` on `TC-284`), the one blocked on **`G27`** (`FR-175`, no host), and the one that is **not test-case shaped** (`FR-161`, an architectural quality). **New §10.5 is generated by [`build_coverage_matrix.py`](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Tools/build_coverage_matrix.py)**, which fails the build on any undeclared hole, and states that *with a case* is not *executable* — `TC-350`–`TC-352` count among the 220 and cannot be run. | 2.6 | Aug 22, 2026 | **§4.1a added — sequence validation, and the order *set*.** Since `Q70` the planning lookup returns **orders, plural**, so *“belongs to the established order”* becomes membership in an **ordered set**. Two validations, both also applied at check-in because a rule enforced at one of two entry points is not enforced (`Q73` item 7): order-set membership `[ORD008]`, and tier order `[ORD004]`. ⚠ **The tier refusal is deliberately stricter than the `Q24` out-of-sequence override** — `Q73`'s own consequence 1 makes staging a multi-order rod early *“refused, not overridden”*, because the boundary that rod carries would have nowhere to run; the `Q24` override still covers a deviation **within** a tier, which is a different thing. Residual: **`Q49`**, whether multi-order-last holds with no weld |
| 1.0 | Jul 29, 2026 | Initial specification: station concept, bay state model, staging validations, traveler queue, three-step wizard, and the two-sequence model. |
| 2.0 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Reissued as version 2.0 for client review.** Applied the July 30, 2026 client decisions: shared coil status set at check-in only; pre-check-out approval determined by weld state, with welded removal a supervisor-authorised rejection to `HOLD`; failed inspection released by WIP rejection; off-schedule staging replaced by automatic line selection; min/max limits for four dimensional attributes; a rod may carry more than one order; bundles are never stacked; no welded-not-checked-in status. Document restructured to client-deliverable form — superseded rules, prior design iterations, internal schema and interface detail, and repository-internal commentary removed. New requirements `PCI009`–`PCI020` proposed for the removal, bay-state, order-resolution and sequence-authorisation rules the SRS does not currently cover. Open items consolidated into Section 11 with a sign-off checklist. New requirement identifiers span `PCI009`–`PCI017`. |
| — | Aug 1, 2026 | **Rejection captured at the station.** The WIP rejection that releases a blocked position is now raised on this screen rather than reached by navigating to a separate one, so the failing rod and its position are already known and the operator returns to a station that has not lost its state. No rule in this document changed. |
| 2.1 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Version 2.1.** Added **Section 8.1 `PCI021`** — a read-only list of the welds already recorded against the run in progress: time, rod pair, footage at the weld, weld type, operator and quality, with the mandatory failure reason on a failed weld (`WLD013`). Scoped to the **current run** (not the shift, not the coil), available whenever a run exists including while the idle position is empty or blocked, and not editable — correcting a recorded weld remains the unspecified `WLD011`. This replaces a station control labelled *Weld event log*, which navigated to the weld-**recording** form; nothing in the system previously listed the welds made during a run, although each is a certificate traceability input. Also recorded in Section 8 that marking the weld does **not** ask for an operator badge — the operator is taken from the signed-in station session, since `WLD003` requires it recorded, not re-entered, and a keyed value could disagree with the session actually stamped. |
| 2.2 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Version 2.2.** Added **Section 8.1 `PCI022` — weld quality.** Recording a weld now **requires** a Pass/Fail result, with a reason mandatory on Fail (`WLD013`), using the same six reasons as the Weld Event screen so a weld is documented identically wherever it is captured. Neither result is pre-selected: this is the check whose purpose is to make the operator look at the join, and a pre-selected Pass can be confirmed without being read. **A failing weld is recorded but does not mark the rod welded** — the join did not hold, so the rod is not joined to the running rod and the line cannot transition through it; the position keeps reading *not yet welded*, the station states that the last weld failed and why, and the operator remakes it. Previously the station recorded only *that* a weld happened, with no statement of whether it held, while the same join captured on the Weld Event screen did record a quality result — one physical join, documented two ways. Renumbered the run weld list to **8.2**. **Q24 widened** rather than a new question raised: a remade weld leaves more than one record of one physical join, which is the re-weld-on-certificate question Q24 already asks — now reachable both by a weld that breaks mid-run and by one that fails its quality check before anything runs through it. |
| 2.3 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Version 2.3. The station-level weld readiness band is removed and every control moves onto the payoff position it acts on.** The band sat between the two positions and the traveler queue, carrying a sentence of narrative and two buttons. Its narrative was already on the position cards — the weight and percentage on the payoff bar, the weld states in the position's alert line, the cold-start message in the empty-position text — so the band restated at station level what the operator was already reading on the card. Its two controls were station-level for no reason other than where they happened to sit. **Mark as welded now sits on the staged position** (Section 8): that position *is* the incoming rod, so the action carries the rod into the record instead of asking which rod is meant. Its unavailable states now state their reason on the card, which the band never did. **Welds this run now sits on the running position** (Section 8.2), because the run belongs to that position, and carries its count on the control. **Open the active run is withdrawn as a position action** (Section 4.1) — the run screen remains reachable from the application bar and the Line Status board, and this station's purpose is preparing the *next* rod rather than driving the current one. The one instruction the band alone carried, *induction-weld tail to head*, is now stated on the staged position whenever a rod is running. **One consequence needs client confirmation** (**Q83**): with the control on the running position, at cold start there is no position to show it on, so *Welds this run* is **absent** rather than shown-and-greyed as it was before. The traveler queue gained the heading **"Rods In Queue"** (Section 4.5) — the queue head had been an unlabelled empty row since the order-context line was removed, leaving the table with no name. Also recorded: where a position has an obvious next step it is emphasised, and **the running position deliberately emphasises nothing**, because both of its actions are exceptional and emphasising either would read as a recommendation. |
| 2.5 | Aug 15, 2026 | **Reissued as version 2.5 — the `## Document Change History` block removed.** The block is gone from the specification and its rows are folded into this section, which now carries a **Version** column; the client `.docx` no longer prints a history section, and the document's version is stated in its header block only. **No requirement, decision, open item or sign-off row changed.** This completes the 12 Aug 2026 consolidation, which had left these thirteen blocks in place as deliverable content. Team sizes spelled as words (*"Three developers"*) are accepted, which the old positional `zip` never had to handle; with one team size the sprint and milestone columns drop their *"— N devs"* labels. **(2)** Coverage checked every backlog work item against the content file, so excluding Phase 12 from the plan failed the build with five errors. **The workbook's scope is the sprint plan, not the backlog** — coverage now runs against the allocation matrix, and a backlog story absent from it is an exclusion rather than an error. **It is printed at the end of every build**, because a story dropped by accident and one removed by decision are otherwise indistinguishable. **(3)** Client wording written for three options was rewritten for one, the sheet renamed **Delivery Summary**, and the excluded scope named on both it and the read-me — a client should not have to infer that yield and costing are absent. |
| 1.1 | Aug 2, 2026 | Plan team | v1.1. Two-status rule and single check-in, per client. Section 3.5 rewritten from a four-status proposal to the confirmed *Ready for FL2* / *Checked in* pair plus the exclusivity rule; Section 3.4 gains the two scan-while-occupied outcomes; rules renumbered SQ-7 to SQ-12; confirmed decisions 6 and 7 added; open item 2 reduced to the stored vocabulary only; open item 6 added, since a quality-held spool has no place on a two-status screen. |
| 1.0 | Aug 2, 2026 | Plan team | Initial issue. New screen: Dashboard 5A, the FL2 spool queue. Records the reasons it is being added, the scan-resolves-order behaviour, the four ways a scan can end, and the five items still needing client input. |
| 1.3 | Aug 15, 2026 | Plan team | **Reissued as version 1.3 — the `## Document Change History` block removed.** The block is gone from the specification and its rows are folded into this section, which now carries a **Version** column; the client `.docx` no longer prints a history section, and the document's version is stated in its header block only. **No requirement, decision, open item or sign-off row changed.** This completes the 12 Aug 2026 consolidation, which had left these thirteen blocks in place as deliverable content. It also closes a drift the earlier pass created: version **1.2** was the 12 Aug repository-wide reissue and never had a row of its own in either place. |
| 1.4 | Aug 20, 2026 | Plan team | **Reissued as version 1.4 — the screen's founding premise is reversed and its central assumption withdrawn.** From the [20 Aug client call](BaseDocuments/ClientCall_2026-08-20_SyncPlan.md). **§1.2 — FL2 now gets pre-check-in**, which this document's whole rationale rested on it *not* having. Recorded with the distinction that makes both statements true: FL2 still has **no staging space**, and what the client asked for is **validation before the spool is fetched**, not a place to put it — so the screen keeps its shape and gains an action. **§8 assumption 1 withdrawn** — *"a spool belongs to at most one order at a time"* is the opposite of what the client confirmed; the presentation it warned would be needed is the one now specified. **§3.2** the order bar becomes a **set** with the operator selecting the one being made, and **any identifier on the FL1 label resolves the spool** — the carrier number or any alpha. **§3.5** gains the **carrier-versus-material** distinction: the spool is a reusable stenciled article that *"is basically free again, back into the pool"* after FL2, and that state belongs to the carrier, not to the material, so it is deliberately **not** a third status on a work queue. **§4** spool identifier becomes the **carrier**, and `Source` lists each rod **with the weight it contributed**, which is what the certificates are built from. New rules **SQ-13**, **SQ-14**; **SQ-12 superseded** (the screen may now write a validation record — shape pending). Six new confirmed decisions **8–13**. **§7 item 1 CLOSED** — open since 2 Aug, and answered on all four counts: the carrier is the reusable physical article, typed and validated, assigned at the FL1 completion transaction, read at FL2 from the high-temp label. Item 2 narrowed. Four new open items **7–10**: what an FL2 pre-check-in records, orders per spool and who selects, whether empty carriers need to be visible anywhere, and the stenciled format. ⚠ **Also removed a stray `Document Change History` row** the 15 Aug consolidation left behind at the foot of the file — the sign-off table's last row was a v1.2 change entry. |

## [MVP-1/RequirementDocuments/WeldEvent.md](MVP-1/ProjectPlan/Business/Screens/WeldEvent.md)

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | Apr 2026 | Initial specification — screen purpose, captured data, traceability chain, confirm behaviour, end-to-end flow, welding-wire requirements. |
| 2.0 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Reissued as version 2.0 for client review.** Weld type corrected to induction only. Added the alloy/temper/diameter match as a stated validation, both payoff positions as captured data, and the July 30 decisions (welded-rod release, no welded-not-checked-in status, no stacking, mid-run coil break). Raised the coil-start footage offset (OI-25) and the in-place weld reversal as blocking client questions. Interface payloads, screen navigation targets and internal schema references removed. |
| 2.2 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Version 2.2 — the Weld Event screen is retired.** Dashboard 4 was removed, and the *Log Weld Event* action was removed from the active-run monitors on **all three lines**. The weld is now recorded **only** at the Rod Pre-Check-In station (Dashboard 2A, *Mark as welded*), which since version 2.1 captures the complete record including the mandatory quality result — this is also where the weld physically happens, so it removes a walk to a separate screen. **Two capabilities were not rehoused:** the re-sequenceable rod queue and the traceability chain view (`FR-175`). **And FL2, which has no pre-check-in station, now has no way to record a weld at all** — correct if FL2 only inherits its spool's weld markers, wrong if it joins spool to spool; the shift summary reports FL2 weld events, so confirmation is needed. Both raised as open items. |
| 2.1 | Aug 1, 2026 | **Version 2.1 — weld quality is captured with the weld.** Added Section 4.1 recording that the weld event is captured wherever the weld is made, with the **same mandatory quality result** in every case — there is no lighter path that records a weld without stating whether it held. Recorded that **a failed weld does not complete the join**: where the incoming rod is pre-checked-in, a Fail leaves it staged and un-welded, and the operator remakes the weld, so only a Pass marks the rod welded. Noted that a remade weld therefore leaves more than one record of one physical join, which widens **Q24** (re-welds on the certificate) to cover a weld that fails at capture and not only one that breaks mid-run; footage attribution across the two boundaries remains **Q22**. |
| 2.4 | Aug 15, 2026 | **Reissued as version 2.4 — the `## Document Change History` block removed.** The block is gone from the specification and its rows are folded into this section, which now carries a **Version** column; the client `.docx` no longer prints a history section, and the document's version is stated in its header block only. **No requirement, decision, open item or sign-off row changed.** This completes the 12 Aug 2026 consolidation, which had left these thirteen blocks in place as deliverable content. It also closes a drift the earlier pass created: version **2.3** was the 12 Aug repository-wide reissue and never had a row of its own in either place. |
